title: Potential bug in read-only `Array` access (invalidated object references).
body:
### Tested versions

`master` (3f56b3b23916ff54a1715cb8444304ce3c50283d) back through 023b1d7f (2022-05-17 / Godot 4.0).

### System information

N/A

### Issue description

`Array.operator[]` currently returns a Variant reference.

Read-only semantics for `Arrays` currently use a single surrogate cache variable in `Array`. On access, the cache will be overridden with the variable to be returned. A reference to it is then returned:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/3f56b3b23916ff54a1715cb8444304ce3c50283d/core/variant/array.cpp#L98-L104

When the array is accessed a second time, the temporary variable `read_only` is overridden with the variable returned. The reference to the first variable thus incorrectly points to the second variable. 

It is not very likely that this bug is triggered often, if at all, but it is a surprise waiting to happen, and possibly overlooked by implementers.

## How to Fix
I see two solutions:
- The behavior could be documented through a comment. This would not fix it, but make it less likely to occur.
- Better, `Array.operator[]` could return a `Variant` copy. `Variant` copies are _relatively fast_. For GDScript access, this should be "Good enough".
    - `Array` should not be stored internally anyway (see https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/102531), so it should not have a noticeable performance impact.

### Steps to reproduce

(not tested, but should trigger the bug)

```c++
Array array;

array.push_back(0);
array.push_back(1);
array.make_read_only();

Variant &a = array[0];
Variant &b = array[1];

print_line(a);  // 1 (incorrect)
print_line(b);  // 1
```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

None.
